839 PM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Issued Coastal Flood Advisory for St. Mary's County. Otherwise,
no other changes were made.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry conditions and seasonable temperatures through early 
  next week, with frost possible this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry conditions and seasonable temperatures through 
early next week, with frost possible this weekend.

Omega block sets up across the CONUS with stout cutoff lows along 
the Western and Eastern coasts. Ridging across the central to 
eastern CONUS will maintain dry conditions over the Mid-Atlantic for 
the foreseeable future. Seasonal temperatures expected as highs 
generally reach the 60s each day, then fall back to the 30s to 40s 
at night. The omega block begins to shift eastward late this week, 
eventually breaking down over the weekend into the start of next 
week. This allows a series of surface high pressure systems to pass 
through the region, with dry cold fronts reinforcing the cooler, 
albeit seasonal, temperatures. One of these highs that passes 
directly overhead Friday into the weekend will allow for strong 
radiational cooling to occur. We could experience colder temps than 
currently forecast Friday night and Saturday night. If temps drop to 
the low to mid 30s along and west of I-95, frost will be possible. A 
slight warm up in temps to around 70F for next Monday and
Tuesday.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected through Thursday with surface 
high pressure overhead. Dry conditions will prevail with light north 
winds today at less than 15 kts switching to the northwest 
Thursday. Highest winds will be at terminals (along and east of I-
95) near the waters with occasional gusts between 15-20 kts mainly 
during the late morning and afternoon hours. Winds will switch to 
the northeast Friday into Saturday at less than 15 kts. 

VFR conditions continue Saturday through Monday with light and 
variable winds expected.

&&

.MARINE...
Prolonged SCA conditions continue through at least Friday morning as 
coastal low pressure pushes further off the Mid-Atlantic coast. 
Small Craft Advisories remain in effect for the Chesapeake Bay and 
lower tidal Potomac through Thursday morning and will likely be 
extended through Friday morning. The threat is highest in the lower 
portions of the waters, with additional Advisories possible through 
Friday evening. Outside of the winds, no hazardous marine conditions 
are expected.

No marine hazards expected Saturday through Monday. Winds light and 
variable through the period.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Elevated tide levels are expected through the weekend as we approach 
the Full Moon on October 26, along with being in King Tide season 
(though we are already past the highest astronomical tides that were 
at the beginning of October). Sensitive locations are forecast to 
reach Action Stage during most of the high tide cycles this week, 
with sensitive locations at Annapolis, Solomons Island, Dahlgren, 
and Alexandria reaching minor tidal flooding. The presence of 
northerly winds is likely to keep tidal flooding within Minor flood 
stage.
